headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Chatwoot’s broad network egress and customer-data handling; the pair otherwise has no shared write or execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. Chatwoot has broad network egress, but python-cheatsheet has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, MCP, or execution surfaces, so there is no clear channel for Chatwoot output to be parsed as instructions by the other agent.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Chatwoot output into python-cheatsheet as prompt text, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared prompt channels.
Disable any copy-paste automation between outputs and inputs.
Use a human review step before reusing Chatwoot text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, messages, and reports, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no data classes touched and no filesystem or network access. The pair lacks a shared workspace, so leakage is not a default pathway; residual risk is limited to manual transfer or external orchestration.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes Chatwoot customer data into python-cheatsheet prompts, leakage can occur.
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside these profiles, the risk increases.
mitigations: Do not paste customer records into the documentation agent.
Use redacted samples for any cross-agent review.
Restrict Chatwoot exports to approved staff only.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on any future shared workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write or mutable-resource capabilities are present. Chatwoot has broad network egress, but python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP, so there is no shared mutable surface for conflict.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is replaced with a writable agent targeting the same resources as Chatwoot, conflict becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Avoid assigning both agents to the same mutable resource.
Separate operational responsibilities by tool class.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are later enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing content and reports, but python-cheatsheet is a reference/documentation agent with no action-taking authority or execution surfaces. That makes direct cascading errors unlikely; the main risk is a human or external system treating Chatwoot output as authoritative without verification.
conditions: IF an operator uses Chatwoot output as source text for downstream decisions without review, errors can cascade.
IF python-cheatsheet is wrapped in an action-taking orchestrator, the severity increases.
mitigations: Require human verification before downstream use.
Mark Chatwoot outputs as untrusted drafts.
Keep python-cheatsheet in documentation-only mode.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any automated action.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and related records, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and appears to have no residency or retention controls documented. The pair creates a compliance gap if regulated customer data is copied into the documentation agent, because the second agent has no stated safeguards or data-handling policy.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is transferred from Chatwoot into python-cheatsheet, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the copied material, the gap becomes material.
mitigations: Do not move regulated data into the documentation agent.
Use anonymized excerpts for documentation tasks.
Document a retention rule for any copied content.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls before sharing sensitive data.
